intro: The Torah is a very long scroll. Its first book is called Bereshit. That means "In the beginning." This unit tells the first stories in that book. You will hear about the very first week, a day of rest, a garden, a big boat, a dove and a rainbow.

Jewish families have read these stories for a very long time. Many families in Chicago read them every year. In this unit we learn what the Torah says. We learn what the stories mean to the people who read them. We do not decide if they are true. We listen and we learn.

By the end, you will be able to tell the story of the first week. You will know what Shabbat is. You will be able to tell the story of Noah, the ark and the rainbow. And you will know what a promise is.
bigQuestion: What do the first stories in the Torah say about the world, rest and promises?

timeline.t: The Torah says God made light, and called it Day and Night
The story says God made the sky
Dry land, the sea and plants
The sun, the moon and the stars
Fish in the sea and birds in the sky
Animals on the land, and then people
The story says God rested; Jewish families call this day Shabbat
Noah builds the ark and the animals come in two by two
Rain falls for forty days and forty nights
The dove brings back an olive leaf; the rainbow is a sign of a promise

words.d: the first five books of the Hebrew Bible, kept as one long scroll
the Hebrew name of the first book of the Torah; it means "In the beginning"
the seventh day of the week, a day of rest for Jewish families
a braided bread that Jewish families eat on Shabbat
the garden in the Torah where the first people lived
the very big boat Noah built in the Torah's story
the bird that brought Noah an olive leaf in the Torah's story
something you say you will do, and then you do it

test.q: How many books are in the Torah?
test.why: The Torah has five books. The first one is Bereshit, or Genesis.
Bereshit is the first word of the Torah. It means "In the beginning."

test.q: What does the Torah say was made on day one?
test.why: On day one, the story says, God said, "Let there be light."

test.q: Who does the Torah say was made last?
test.why: People were made last, at the end of day six.

test.q: What do Jewish families call the seventh day?
test.why: Shabbat is the Jewish day of rest, from Friday night to Saturday night.
Challah is the braided bread Jewish families eat on Shabbat.
In the Torah's story, the ark is the very big boat Noah built.

test.q: How long did it rain in Noah's story?
test.why: The Torah says it rained forty days and forty nights.

test.q: What did the dove bring back to Noah?
test.why: The dove brought an olive leaf. It showed the water was going down.

test.q: What does the Torah say the rainbow is a sign of?
choices: A promise never to flood the whole earth again
test.why: The Torah says the rainbow is a sign of God's promise to Noah and the earth.

write.prompt: Pick one story from this unit: the first week (Genesis 1–2) or Noah (Genesis 6–9). Draw or write what the Torah says happened. Then tell one thing Jewish families do to remember it, like Shabbat candles or the rainbow blessing.
tips: Say which book and story you picked, like "Genesis 1, the first week."
Say "the Torah says" when you tell what the story says.
Say "Jewish families" when you tell what people do to remember it.
Use two words from the unit, like Shabbat, ark or promise.
